chapter: The China offer, wedding and Shanghai
title: Madame Sun Yat-sen's dancing lessons
summary: A sister of Madame Chiang came on Saturdays for dance lessons from trombonist Duke Upshaw and testified at the trial.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Oh he was? Didn't you tell me once that Madame Ch'iang Kai Chek was trying to learn to tap dance?
[Yes,] she would come down every Saturday afternoon and Duke Upshaw who was one of the trombone players in the band was a good dancer.

Yes. He was teaching her how to dance. Every Saturday she'd come down and spend a couple of hours learning how to dance. So you know, we were all pretty close together. And she and I'm so glad that she was there that night that this happened. So she testified and so on.
*Madam Soon Yat Sen, the sister of Madam Chiang Kai Chek, was taking dancing lessons.---Clayton.
And by this time was she married to .... General Ching.
Oh she was, so she was an important person then?
Yes, very important. Both of them.
Well that's very interesting. That was, two very striking incidents in your life. The departure for Japan and.....
